turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - cdft_piezo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose
    properties are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal chemistry,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the LARGEST piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij| (in
pC/N), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The piezoelectric strain tensor \(d_{ij}\) is identically zero in any centrosymmetric crystal. Among the non-centrosymmetric candidates the largest coefficients occur when three crystal-chemical factors act together: (i) a polar (or at least non-centrosymmetric) structure that lies close to a higher-symmetry prototype, implying a soft polar phonon, (ii) stereochemically active lone pairs that generate anomalously large Born charges, and (iii) a mechanically soft lattice (halides or thiophosphates rather than oxides or nitrides) so that \(d=e\cdot C^{-1}\) is amplified.

These conditions are optimally satisfied by the distorted \({\rm ABX}_3\) halide perovskites that contain \(\mathrm{Ge}^{2+}\) or \(\mathrm{In}^{+}\):
- c025 and c026 (\(\mathrm{InGeCl}_3\)) and c041 (\(\mathrm{KGeCl}_3\)) are rhombohedral or triclinic perovskites whose B-site cations carry lone pairs. Their lattice parameters remain close to cubic, the polar displacements are modest (\(\sim0.3\,\text{Å}\)), and the Cl framework is far softer than any oxide analogue. Consequently both the piezoelectric stress constants \(e_{ij}\) and the compliances are large, producing the highest \(|d_{ij}|\).
- c073 (\(\mathrm{KBiP}_2\mathrm{S}_6\)) combines a Bi lone pair with a soft thiophosphate lattice and a distinctly polar packing, giving the next-largest response.
- c011 (\(\mathrm{KCaCl}_3\)) is a similarly under-distorted chloride perovskite; even without a lone pair the proximity to cubic symmetry and the low elastic moduli still yield a sizable \(d_{ij}\).

All other families (wurtzites, zincblendes, molecular crystals, ordinary oxides) lack at least one of the three factors and are therefore expected to exhibit substantially smaller maximum strain coefficients.

Final: c025, c026, c041, c073, c011
